chunks: I heard our master Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: Verily, an angel descends from the sky every night carrying three mithqals of musk from the musk of Paradise, and he casts it into the Euphrates. And there is no river in the east of the earth nor in its west with a greater blessing than it.

key_terms.الْفُرَاتِ: Al-Furat (Euphrates) — the major river of Iraq, considered especially sacred in Shia tradition
key_terms.بَرَكَةً: Blessing (baraka) — divine favor and spiritual benefit
key_terms.مَثَاقِيلَ: Mithqals — a traditional unit of weight (approx. 4.25 grams each); used to indicate a precise, generous measure
key_terms.مِسْكِ الْجَنَّةِ: Musk of Paradise — the finest, most fragrant substance, signifying the spiritual purity and divine blessing infused into the river

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the Euphrates River and its blessings?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) attests to the sacred status of the Euphrates River, describing how an angel nightly deposits musk from Paradise into it, making it the most blessed river on earth. This tradition reflects early Islamic cosmology and the special veneration of the Euphrates — a river flowing through Iraq, historically linked to the tragedies of Karbala — among Shia communities. The hadith would have resonated deeply with the Imam's audience as a reminder of God's continued grace upon a land of immense spiritual significance.
